question: A quantity is represented by $Q(t)=at^2+bt$. Its instantaneous rates of change at $t=1$ and $t=2$ are $7$ and $11$, respectively. Determine $a$ and $b$, and hence find its instantaneous rate at $t=3$.
explanation: Rate functionDifferentiating $Q(t)=at^2+bt$ gives$$\frac{dQ}{dt}=2at+b$$Condition at $t=1$$$2a+b=7$$Condition at $t=2$$$4a+b=11$$Determination of the parametersSubtracting the first equation from the second gives$$2a=4\Rightarrow a=2$$Substituting in $2a+b=7$,$$4+b=7\Rightarrow b=3$$Rate at $t=3$$$\left.\frac{dQ}{dt}\right|_{t=3}=2(2)(3)+3=15$$Final resultThe parameters are $a=2$ and $b=3$, and the instantaneous rate at $t=3$ is $15$ units per unit time.
